note: Subset Constraint Dictionary (internal-docs Bagian 4). MVP-1 hanya domain yang paling sering muncul di persona target. v0.2: + C6.4 Response/Follow-up Failure, verdict taxonomy (STOP/NOT_YET/TEST_FIRST), disqualifiers.

verdicts.STOP: Jangan lakukan aksi di area ini sama sekali
verdicts.TEST_FIRST: Jangan scale dulu — uji dengan volume kecil terukur, perbaiki proses, baru naikkan

D1.2.name: Goal-Path Ambiguity
D1.2.definition: Tujuan ada tapi jalur menuju tujuan tidak terdefinisi.

V2.1.name: Capability-Offer Disconnect
V2.1.definition: Kemampuan ada, tapi belum diubah menjadi penawaran yang bisa dibeli.

V2.4.name: Value-Proof Gap
V2.4.definition: Klaim nilai tidak didukung bukti hasil yang bisa diverifikasi.

M3.1.name: ICP Dilution
M3.1.definition: Sasaran terlalu luas — tidak ada segmen spesifik yang paling cocok membeli.

M3.4.name: Authority Mismatch
M3.4.definition: Kontak yang dijangkau bukan pemegang keputusan pembelian.

DS4.2.name: Distribution Inactivity
DS4.2.definition: Tidak ada aktivitas outreach yang konsisten ke calon pembeli.

DM5.1.name: Demand Insufficiency
DM5.1.definition: Demand terbukti ada, tapi volume pipeline belum cukup untuk menutup gap ke target revenue.

DM5.5.name: Trust Deficit
DM5.5.definition: Pasar tidak cukup percaya untuk bertransaksi.

disqualifiers.source_prose: Ada transaksi nyata baru-baru ini (trust terbukti cukup)
disqualifiers.note: Disqualifier terpicu: ada transaksi nyata baru-baru ini — trust terbukti cukup; 'Trust Deficit' kemungkinan bukan akar masalah

disqualifiers.source_prose: Tidak ada bukti rejection/loss yang disebabkan trust/proof
disqualifiers.reason: Menuntut kategorisasi semantik 'rejection akibat trust/proof' yang belum ada di bahasa predikat generik. Kandidat: absennya evidence pada mechanism `trust_gap`. Belum dieksekusi karena akan mengubah status DM5.5 di artefak dan butuh keputusan owner — dinyatakan NON-EKSEKUTABEL supaya deklarasi tidak diam-diam inert (ontology v0.3).

DM5.6.name: Proof Deficit
DM5.6.definition: Tidak ada bukti sosial / hasil nyata yang memperkuat klaim.

C6.1.name: Qualification Failure
C6.1.definition: Percakapan terjadi dengan pihak yang tidak akan pernah membeli.

C6.3.name: Value Framing Failure
C6.3.definition: Nilai tidak dikomunikasikan dalam bahasa masalah pembeli.

C6.4.name: Response/Follow-up Failure
C6.4.definition: Inquiry/prospek masuk tetapi bocor karena respons lambat atau follow-up tidak dilakukan.

R7.2.name: Onboarding Friction
R7.2.definition: Customer gagal mencapai nilai pertama karena onboarding berat.

L8.1.name: Time-for-Money Trap
L8.1.definition: Revenue hanya tumbuh sebanding jam kerja — tidak ada leverage.

L8.3.name: Delivery Capacity Constraint
L8.3.definition: Kapasitas delivery sudah mendekati maksimum: menambah klien tanpa mengubah cara kerja/asisten tidak bisa dilayani.

classes_v04.note: Ontology v0.4 candidate classes (iter-12) — dipakai saat constraint ontology tidak cukup (lihat NO_FIT di agents/diagnosis.py). Belum ber-status constraint sampai divalidasi pada >=3 kasus.

process_gaps.name: Process Gap
process_gaps.definition: Proses operasional yang tidak ada/terputus — bukan akar kausal, tapi penyebab mekanis kebocoran.

commercialization_maturity.name: Commercialization Maturity Gap
commercialization_maturity.definition: Kapabilitas & demand sudah ada, tetapi sistem komersial belum cukup standar untuk mereproduksi hasil.

levels.L3: Repeatable offer — penawaran bisa dijelaskan berulang

D1.*.text: Don't pick any growth tactic yet
D1.*.reason: The route to your goal is not defined yet. Any tactic runs without direction, and your energy spreads in many directions at once
D1.*.until: One route (channel, ideal client and offer) is chosen on purpose and written in one sentence

V2.*.reason: Ads multiply your message. If the offer has not been tested, you multiply noise at a cost
V2.*.until: A test of the evidence or the offer has met its success measure

DS4.*.text: Don't build lots of content yet
DS4.*.reason: Content with no direct contact with likely buyers is a tower with no door: your energy runs out before any conversation starts. Do direct outreach in small volume first, content follows
DS4.*.until: A direct outreach routine has been running for at least 2 weeks

M3.*.reason: Your target is not sharp yet. Adding channels before your ideal client is clear only widens the shots in the wrong direction
M3.*.until: One ideal-client segment is defined and tested with at least 1 real conversation

DM5.*.text: Don't scale how you win clients, and don't assume demand is enough: measure it first from what you already have
DM5.*.reason: Demand existing is not the same as demand being enough. Before judging whether you need more, measure how many inquiries become deals among the leads you already have. A test is not scale: run a small test to learn what converts, not to add volume
DM5.*.until: Your numbers are measured (inquiry, call, proposal, close) and the number of deals your target needs can be worked out from data, not assumption

R7.*.reason: The value leaks after the first month: more traffic widens the leak, not revenue
R7.*.until: Existing clients reach a second value (repeat work or a measured result)

C6.*.text: Don't scale how you win clients yet, and don't test volume at the same time as fixing conversion. Do it in 4 phases: (1) fix price response on the leads you have, (2) measure how many inquiries become deals, (3) then run a controlled test with about 10 targeted prospects, (4) then judge whether the target is feasible
C6.*.reason: A test is not scale, and an order is not parallel. If fixing conversion and testing volume run together and fail, you cannot tell why (price? ideal client? demand?). First close the leak on the live leads you already have, measure, then add volume
C6.*.until: Each phase passes before the next: phases 1 and 2 until conversion is measured, phase 3 until at least 1 deal closes from the small test, phase 4 judges whether the target is realistic

L8.*.reason: Your capacity and process are not repeatable yet: more clients cost you quality and health. If the limit is delivery capacity (L8.3), speed up by handing off the work that can be handed off before adding clients
L8.*.until: Your delivery process is written down and has been run again without you at full stretch (or part of the work has been handed off)
